title: Week four review
grammarFocus: Only what you can already say
listenFocus: Re-listen to a story from this week
practiceFocus: Speak for 5–10 minutes entirely in Spanish

points.title: Nothing new
points.rule: Reuse only what you can already say. Regular preterite for a trip: viajé, viajamos, salió, salieron. The four irregular preterites in every person: fui, hice, tuve, estuve. The imperfect for background and habit: jugaba, vivíamos, era. Both together: estaba… cuando…. Commands: corta, no cocines, hable. The future: viajaré, tendré, haré.

grammar.notYet: Any new tense or pattern. Today is for speaking, not a new chart.

phrases.spanish: El año pasado viajé a Portugal con mi familia.
phrases.english: Last year I travelled to Portugal with my family.

phrases.spanish: Fuimos a la playa e hizo mucho sol.
phrases.english: We went to the beach and it was very sunny.

phrases.spanish: Cuando era niño, vivía cerca del mar.
phrases.english: When I was a child, I used to live near the sea.

phrases.spanish: Estaba durmiendo cuando llegaron mis amigos.
phrases.english: I was asleep when my friends arrived.

phrases.spanish: Corta la fruta y añade un poco de azúcar.
phrases.english: Cut the fruit and add a bit of sugar.

phrases.spanish: El próximo año viajaré más y trabajaré menos.
phrases.english: Next year I will travel more and work less.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Este mes viajé a la costa. Hizo un tiempo increíble.
lines.english: This month I travelled to the coast. The weather was amazing.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: No, fui con mi hermano. Cuando éramos niños, íbamos allí cada verano.
lines.english: No, I went with my brother. When we were kids, we used to go there every summer.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Tendré más trabajo, pero también viajaré a ver a mis padres.
lines.english: I will have more work, but I will also travel to see my parents.

practice.title: Ten minutes, a month of change
practice.instruction: Speak for five to ten minutes. Cover a past trip or event, one childhood memory, a short anecdote combining both pasts, one instruction or piece of advice, and one plan for next year.
tips: Move between tenses without stopping to name them.
If you are not sure which past to use, ask whether this is the event or the background.
